JUDGEMENT CALLS - the five middle-row crossings S18, S16, S12, S11, S10
  These are the only genuinely ambiguous intersections on the sheet: each is a deg-4 place where a vertical rail carrying two components crosses the middle row. There is not a single hop or jog anywhere in this drawing, so the drafter has no drawn 'not connected' notation. All five are recorded as JUNCTIONS. Reasoning, in the order the brief prescribes:
  (1) Electrical impossibility rules out the all-crossings reading. The middle row overshoots ~27px to the LEFT of the left rail and simply stops at (35,533) - verified by zoom, it is a dead pen overshoot, not a wire to anything. If both S18 (64,533) and S16 (304,513) were crossings, the middle-row segment from that dead end to Capacitor #7's left lead would carry exactly one terminal (7.0). So at least one of S18/S16 - both plain bare X's - has to be a junction, which establishes that on this sheet a bare X can be a junction.
  (2) Given that, the ink prior applies uniformly: all five are plain crossings with no hop and no jog, so all five are junctions. Any mixed reading would have the drafter using the identical mark to mean two different things within one row.
  (3) The one thing pulling the other way is S10 (794,476), which does carry a real solder blob: inkmap shows the ink swelling to ~13px across and ~11px tall against a 3-4px stroke, i.e. about 3x the stroke width in both axes, while S11 / S12 / S16 / S18 show no swelling at all (dot scores 1.6 / 2.1 / 1.6 / 1.8 versus 2.7 at S10, and for calibration the unambiguous T at S2 scores 2.1). Under the drafter's-habit rule that would argue the four bare ones are crossings - but that reading is the one (1) rules out. I read the S10 blob as an emphasis dot / ink pooling rather than a discriminator; it agrees with the junction reading anyway.
  Consequence of the other reading: taking S16, S12, S11 as crossings (with S18 forced to stay a junction) would split n4/n5/n6 into six smaller nets - {Zener #2 bottom, Diode #11 top}, {Diode #4 bottom, Zener #10 top}, {Zener #6 bottom, Diode #14 top} as isolated column pairs, and would leave the middle row as a bare chain V-AC/I-DC node - Capacitor #7 - Inductor #8 - Resistor #12, giving 13 nets instead of 10. Everything else in the file is unaffected by that choice. This is the one call on this image I would flag for a second opinion.
